title: Split Array by Prime Indices
summary: Given an integer array nums, divide it into two arrays A and B where A contains elements at prime indices and B contains the rest.
statement: Given an integer array nums, divide it into two arrays A and B where A contains elements at prime indices and B contains the rest. Return the absolute difference between the sums of A and B.
constraints: The array has up to 100,000 signed values.
Indices are zero-based; zero and one are not prime.
Return the absolute difference between prime-index and other-index sums.
hints: Membership depends on index primality, not the stored value.
Sieve prime indices once, then accumulate the two groups.
Sum values at prime indices and subtract the complementary sum.
The sieve classifies every index exactly once, so the two sums form a complete partition.
editorial: The sieve classifies every index exactly once, so the two sums form a complete partition.

tests.explanation: Only index two is prime, producing |4-(2+3)|=1.
Prime indices two and three sum to seven; the other indices sum to four.
